h: פָּרָשַׁת אַחֲרֵי מוֹת, ט׳ Acharei Mos, 9
Every Shabbos Renews the Torah Life Within Our Food

p: he merits to arouse the primordial light,
which is "the light, that it was good."
And this is what it says,
for according to the holy Zohar
וְכֵן הוּא בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה יז
and so it is in Bereishis Rabbah, beginning of chapter 17,
וְאַף לְדַעַת הַגְּמָרָא (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לב, א)
And even according to the Gemara (Rosh Hashanah 32a),
"Let there be light" is the second utterance,
the utterance "Behold, I have given you
אֶת כָּל עֵשֶׂב וְגוֹ׳ (בְּרֵאשִׁית א, כט)
is counted as the tenth utterance according to the Gemara
and as the ninth utterance according to the holy Zohar;
for the utterance "Be fruitful and multiply," etc.,
is not counted as an utterance,
"It is not good for man to be alone," etc.;
but since it is not written
in the utterance "Be fruitful and multiply"
it is not counted as an utterance
"for you it shall be for food":
for it is written, "and it was so,"
for then it became food for man;
was made fit as food for animals;
and before, it was not at all
neither for man nor for animals.
corresponding to the attribute of Malchus.
And even according to the count of the holy Zohar,
in which it is counted the ninth utterance,
it is according to what it says,
"And the advantage of the land is in everything,"
for the completeness of the attribute of Malchus
is when it joins with the attribute of Yesod,
"and from there goes forth benefit to the world,"
And this is as written in the holy Zohar
one spirit from the source of life,
and all provision of this body;
and this is the secret of
'And the advantage of the land is in everything.'"
For "land" is the name of the attribute of Malchus,
and "land" is the name of the body,
as they said in the Gemara (Sanhedrin 91b):
for the body was created from this attribute;
"for the blood is in the nefesh,"
is the spirit for this body.
And this is what is written in the holy Zohar
and this is what is joined, etc.,
'And she gives food to her household':
which rides upon this nefesh," etc.
And the main sustaining of life
that Hashem Yisbarach puts into the food,
כִּי עַל מוֹצָא פִי ה׳ וְגוֹ׳
but by what comes forth from the mouth of Hashem," etc.;
and as written in the holy sefarim,
that it is the words of Torah and the holiness
that Hashem Yisbarach puts into the food.
And this was done on the sixth day,
which corresponds to the attribute of Yesod,
when it was said "and it was so";
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג נח, א)
and as written in the holy Zohar (III 58a):
to give them their food in its time' (Tehillim 104:27).
This is the time of the tzaddik;
who is called the time of the tzaddik, etc.;
and this secret we have established:
עֵינֵי כֹל אֵלֶיךָ יְשַׂבֵּרוּ וְגוֹ׳ (תְּהִלִּים קמה, טו)
'The eyes of all look to You,'" etc. (Tehillim 145:15).
to give them their food in its time,"
which refers to the food of animals;
"The eyes of all look to You,
And this is as we said,
where it is written "and it was so,"
was made fit as food for animals;
and before, they were not fit at all
and for life to be sustained by them.
through the joining of Yesod and Malchus,
which is the completeness of the attribute of Malchus,
and then "she gives food to her household."
Hashem Yisbarach gives a new holiness,
"a soul in which there is all completeness,
after the pattern of the World to Come"
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זוֹהַר חֵלֶק ב פח, ב)
it would not be fitting to call it "bride,"
for she is not called by this name
except during the seven days of feasting,
that it be fit for human food;
And in truth, the essence of life
and this is "Come, eat of my bread," etc.
And so the words of Torah
that Hashem Yisbarach puts into the food,
from these comes the sustaining of life.
the Torah was given on Shabbos,
there is a new bestowal of words of Torah,
and there is a bestowal of blessing upon food,
that there be the sustaining of life.
at the night meal we say,
And this is what is written in the holy Zohar,
"She rises while it is still night
and gives food to her household,"

paragraphs.text: Source: Rosh Hashanah 32a — “״ויאמר״ דבראשית תשעה הוו! ״בראשית״ נמי מאמר הוא, דכתיב: ״בדבר ה׳ שמים נעשו״.” (Oz Vehadar print, p. 75) — “The Gemara asks: Does it refer to the repetition of the phrase: “And He said” in Genesis? There are only nine such phrases, not ten. The Gemara answers that the phrase “In the beginning” is also considered an utterance, as …”
